text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The government is expected to discuss the structure of revenues and expenditures of the 1997 state budget at its session today.
- The government is expected to present the draft law on the next year's state budget to parliament by November 15.
- Juraj Rencko, a leading economist of the Slovak Prognostic Bureau, said the country's economic problems were not as critical as to require a devaluation of the crown.

- The market in privatisation bonds has so far not reflected the recent government ruling banning trading with the bonds with financial settlement outside the official organiser of trading, the O-T-C bourse RM-System.
- Jozef Moravcik, leader of the oposition Democratic Union (DU) and former prime minister, said the new government after the next election would be created by the current parliamentary opposition.
- Slovakia imports some 80 percent of its primary energy sources.

- Slovakia's largest sugar producer Juhocukor said it planned to invest around 250 million crowns this year to increase production to 6,000 tonnes a day from the current 4,000 tonnes. In 1995 Juhocukor accounted for 20 percent of the domestic market, with production totalling 40,250 tonnes.
- The National Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, has approved privatisation of another 21 state companies. The sale totalled around 635 million crowns.

- ZOS Vrutky, which modernises and reconstructs trains, said it planned to become an engineering firm with a wider range of activities due to financial problems of its main customer, state-run Slovak Railways. ZOS revenues in the first nine months of this year totalled 993 million crowns.
- Private airline Air Slovakia said the number of its passengers will for the first time exceed 100,000 this year.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Finance Ministry expects the foreign trade deficit to total 37.7 billion crowns this year, and 61.3 billion crowns in 1997.

SME - The Interior Ministry is expected to present on Tuesday conclusions of the investigation into a tape recording of an alleged conversation between former interior minister Ludovit Hudek and the head of the SIS intelligence service Ivan Lexa, in which the two discussed sacking the second investigator to probe the kidnapping of the president son.
- The ministry is also expected to present on Tuesday conclusions of an investigation of a car blast that this spring killed a former policeman linked to the abduction case.
- University teachers demand an immediate 40 percent pay rise. The teachers said the increase would cost the state budget some 790 million crowns a year.
